solutions.check: grid rebuilt from the blog's light list (unique); every answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

clue.text: Practise heartless commendation

indicators.note: without its heart means the two central letters of the word are removed

explanation.surface: A coach gives grudging, cold-hearted approval during a training session.
explanation.walkthrough: 'heartless' removes CT, the middle two letters of PRACTISE.
explanation.definitionFit: Both words mean expressed approval or admiration, so they are synonyms.

clue.text: Question family's potential fairy tale transport

parts.note: to pump someone is to question them persistently
kin means family or relatives

explanation.surface: Someone asks whether their relatives could travel by fairy-tale carriage.
explanation.walkthrough: In Cinderella, the fairy godmother turns a garden vegetable into her coach, hence 'potential'.
explanation.definitionFit: In the Cinderella story the vegetable becomes a coach, so it is transport waiting to happen.

clue.text: Conscious of fighting in A&E

indicators.note: in means the fighting goes inside the two letters

parts.note: the letters A and E of the hospital department name
war is fighting between nations

explanation.surface: A patient knows about a brawl breaking out in the hospital's Accident and Emergency department.
explanation.definitionFit: Being mindful or cognisant of something is the adjective's meaning, used with 'of'.

clue.text: Walked slowly to arrange date with nurse

indicators.note: arrange means putting these letters into a new order

explanation.surface: A man strolls along to set up an evening out with a nurse.
explanation.walkthrough: 'arrange' looks like setting up a date, but it rearranges DATE and NURSE together.
explanation.definitionFit: Strolled or ambled: walking at a leisurely pace is the verb's sense.

clue.text: Doctor accepts foreign money given by a senior citizen

indicators.note: accepts means the first piece takes the second inside it

parts.note: GP, a general practitioner, is a family doctor in Britain
the rand is the currency of South Africa

explanation.surface: A physician takes payment in another currency from an elderly patient.
explanation.walkthrough: 'given by' is only a link: the A goes on at the end.
explanation.definitionFit: A grandfather is typically an older person, so the word is used loosely for any old man.

clue.text: Looks wide-eyed and searches the internet when it's midnight for love

indicators.note: for means one letter stands in place of another

parts.note: to google is to search online
love is zero in tennis, which looks like the letter O
the middle of the word night is its letter G

explanation.surface: Someone stares in amazement and goes online at the dead of night looking for romance.
explanation.walkthrough: 'midnight' is the letter in the middle of 'night', which replaces one O in GOOGLES.
explanation.definitionFit: To stare with eyes wide open in surprise is the verb's sense, as in ogling.

clue.text: In the middle of wanting some — dream on Geri!

indicators.note: wanting some means the phrase is lacking some of its letters, leaving a run of them inside

parts.note: the letters run across the end of one word into the next

explanation.surface: A fan who longs to be in the thick of it is told to dream on about the Spice Girl Geri.
explanation.walkthrough: The draft took 'In the middle of wanting' as the definition, but 'wanting' adds nothing to the meaning; it pairs with 'some' to signal the hidden letters.
explanation.definitionFit: Surrounded by or amid is a preposition meaning the same as in the middle of.

clue.text: Dad's squiffy with cider — trashed!

indicators.note: squiffy is British slang for slightly drunk, so the letters stagger into a new order

explanation.surface: Father is tipsy on cider and has got completely drunk.
explanation.walkthrough: 'trashed' looks like slang for drunk, but means thrown away.
explanation.definitionFit: Thrown away or binned: to trash something is to throw it out.

clue.text: Help beast of burden first

parts.note: an ass or donkey carries loads
1st is the short form of first, read as IST

explanation.surface: A plea to aid the pack animal before anything else.
explanation.walkthrough: The figure 1 in 1st is read as the letter I.
explanation.definitionFit: To aid or lend a hand is a synonym of the verb.

clue.text: Steal the Spanish coin

parts.note: nick is British slang for steal
el is the Spanish word for the

explanation.surface: Someone is pinching money from Spain.
explanation.definitionFit: In the US and Canada the five-cent piece goes by the name of its metal.

clue.text: Ascertaining the size of plastic geraniums

indicators.note: plastic means mouldable, so these letters can be reshaped into a new order

explanation.surface: Someone is checking how big some artificial flowers are.
explanation.walkthrough: 'plastic' looks like a description of fake flowers, but it signals the anagram of GERANIUMS.
explanation.definitionFit: Finding out dimensions is what a tape or ruler is used for: a direct gloss of the verb.

clue.text: Originally on active service in safe haven

indicators.note: originally means taking what comes at the start of each of the following words

explanation.surface: A soldier on active duty finds himself in a place of safety.
explanation.definitionFit: A desert watering place is a refuge, and figuratively any peaceful retreat or sanctuary.

clue.text: Len's back being embraced by Katie, we hear, and prepared to propose

indicators.note: being embraced by means the reversed name goes inside the letters from Katie
we hear says the letters are taken from how the name sounds when spoken

parts.note: the name Katie is said like the two letters K and T

indicators.note: back means the name is read in the opposite direction

parts.note: Len is a man's name; the 's is read as 'is'

explanation.surface: Len's turned his back on Katie as she hugs him, just as he was about to ask her to marry him.
explanation.walkthrough: The name Katie, spoken, sounds like the two letters K and T. 'Len's' is read as 'Len is'.
explanation.definitionFit: A traditional marriage proposal is made down on one knee, so going down on it is getting ready to ask.

clue.text: Run amok, girls, for the Stones substitute

indicators.note: the letters run amok, careering about wildly into a new order

explanation.surface: Girls go wild in place of the Rolling Stones at a gig.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Run amok' reads as one phrase, but only 'Run' signals the anagram; 'amok' joins 'girls' as fodder. A stone is an old British weight of 14 pounds, used for body weight.
explanation.definitionFit: Metric units of mass replace imperial weights such as stones and pounds.

clue.text: Alan Turing not half upset, it's normal

indicators.note: upset means these letters are knocked over into a new order
not half means only the front half of the surname is kept

explanation.surface: The famous codebreaker Alan Turing is quite distressed, but that's only natural.
explanation.walkthrough: 'not half' leaves TUR from Turing; 'upset' rearranges ALAN with TUR.
explanation.definitionFit: Something ordinary and to be expected is described as what comes naturally: the two words are synonyms.

clue.text: Care team swimming in a river

indicators.note: in means the rearranged letters go inside the river's name

parts.note: the Trent is a major river in the English Midlands

indicators.note: swimming means the letters are moving about into a new order

explanation.surface: A medical team is out swimming in a river.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Care' looks like part of the surface, but it is the definition, in its medical sense.
explanation.definitionFit: Medical care given to a patient is a synonym of the noun.

clue.text: Spent a penny in deserted Salisbury — fast!

indicators.note: in means the euphemism goes inside the letters left from the city
deserted means emptied, so only the outside letters of the city remain

parts.note: to spend a penny is a British euphemism for urinating, from the old coin-operated public toilets

explanation.surface: Someone urgently relieved themselves in an empty Salisbury, an English cathedral city.
explanation.walkthrough: 'deserted' empties Salisbury to SY.
explanation.definitionFit: Quick and rapid are synonyms of the adjective; something done fast is done in a hurry.

clue.text: Bride hung around fringe city

indicators.note: around means the letters are moved about into a new order

explanation.surface: A bride lingered about the outskirts of town.
explanation.walkthrough: 'fringe' looks like the edge of a city, but refers to the Fringe, the huge arts festival held each August in Scotland's capital.
explanation.definitionFit: The capital of Scotland hosts the world-famous Fringe festival each summer.

clue.text: Painful offer

definitions.meaning: sore to the touch, as a bruise is
to put forward formally, as with a bid or resignation

explanation.definitionFit: One sense is sore and sensitive; the other is to submit a formal bid or payment.

clue.text: Get easier with left movement

indicators.note: movement means the letters are shifted into a new order

explanation.surface: A political shift to the left makes things simpler.
explanation.definitionFit: To get a joke is to understand it, which is to become aware of its meaning.

clue.text: Pigs briefly led astray in scam

indicators.note: briefly means cut short, dropping the final letter

parts.note: swine is another word for pigs

indicators.note: astray means the letters go off course into a new order

explanation.surface: Farm animals wander off in some kind of fraud.
explanation.walkthrough: 'briefly' cuts SWINE to SWIN; 'astray' rearranges LED to DLE.
explanation.definitionFit: A con or fraud that cheats people out of money is a synonym of the noun.

clue.text: Outline small vessel

parts.note: S is the abbreviation for small, as in clothing sizes
a ketch is a two-masted sailing boat

explanation.definitionFit: A rough drawing or a brief summary gives a general idea of something.

clue.text: Put up before court judge ruled finally

parts.note: ere is an old word for before

indicators.note: finally means take the closing letter of each of the two words

explanation.surface: Something was set up before the judge in court gave a final ruling.
explanation.definitionFit: A building or tent is put up when it is constructed or raised upright.

clue.text: Bishop shockingly aided law breaker?

parts.note: B is the chess abbreviation for bishop

indicators.note: shockingly means the letters are jolted into a new order

explanation.surface: A churchman scandalously helped someone who broke the law.
explanation.walkthrough: The question mark marks a loose definition: a villain, especially in a film, need not have broken any law.
explanation.definitionFit: A villain or wrongdoer, a word mostly used of fictional bad guys.

clue.text: Make changes to neat arrangement every second

parts.note: to alter something is to make changes to it

indicators.note: an arrangement of the letters puts them in a new order

explanation.surface: Someone is tinkering with a tidy display constantly.
explanation.walkthrough: 'arrangement' rearranges NEAT to NATE. 'every second' looks like it means constantly, but it is the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: Occurring on every other one, skipping one each time, is the adjective's sense.

clue.text: Refrigerator missing top shelf

indicators.note: missing top means the first letter of the word is dropped, the top of a down answer

parts.note: fridge is the short form of refrigerator

explanation.surface: A fridge has lost its uppermost rack.
explanation.walkthrough: 'shelf' looks like part of the fridge, but it is the definition: a ledge of rock or the sea bed.
explanation.definitionFit: A ridge is a raised strip or ledge, as of rock, like a continental shelf.

clue.text: Baby's first dribble is the hard stuff

indicators.note: first means take the opening letter of the word before it

parts.note: to ooze is to dribble or seep out slowly

explanation.surface: An infant's earliest drool is described as strong liquor.
explanation.definitionFit: Strong spirits are called the hard stuff, and slang for alcoholic drink covers them.

clue.text: Listens to some cheesy e-book review

indicators.note: review is read as re-view, looking back, so the run of letters goes backwards
some means only part of the letters in the words are taken

explanation.surface: A critic writes a few words about a corny digital book.
explanation.walkthrough: 'some' takes SYEBO from 'cheesy e-book', and 'review' turns it round.
explanation.definitionFit: To do as told is to heed or comply, the sense of listening to someone.

clue.text: Fear father's taking note

indicators.note: taking means the first piece takes the second inside it

parts.note: dad is an informal word for father
re is the second note of the sol-fa scale

explanation.surface: A parent is anxious about being handed a written message.
explanation.definitionFit: Great apprehension or terror is a synonym of the noun or verb.

clue.text: Rock concert to include Elgar's finale after Verdi's? That must be wrong

indicators.note: after means the following part comes behind the letter from Verdi

parts.note: Verdi's finale, the last letter of the composer's name

indicators.note: to include means the rearranged letters take another letter inside
to rock is to shake, so these letters are shaken into a new order
finale means the closing letter of the composer's name

explanation.surface: A rock gig that features the closing bars of Elgar after Verdi's must be a mistake.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Rock' rearranges CONCERT to NCORECT; 'to include' puts R, Elgar's last letter, inside it, and 'after' puts all that behind I, Verdi's last letter.
explanation.definitionFit: Not accurate or not true: the two words are direct synonyms.

clue.text: Radical old meter fixed

parts.note: ex means former, as in an ex-wife

indicators.note: fixed means repaired, so these letters are put right into a new order

explanation.surface: An outdated gas or electricity meter has been mended in some revolutionary way.
explanation.walkthrough: 'fixed' rearranges METER to TREME.
explanation.definitionFit: Political views far from the centre are called both radical and immoderate.

clue.text: Pursued innocent by phone

indicators.note: by phone means the word is heard spoken, not seen written

parts.note: chaste means pure and innocent

explanation.surface: Someone harmless was followed up through phone calls.
explanation.definitionFit: Ran after or hunted down: the past tense matches the clue's verb.
